title: Special consideration after illness
scenario: Synthetic scenario: imagine a student was sick during an exam and wants to understand what general evidence may be needed. Use Uni-Navigator to inspect the answer and decide whether staff contact is needed. Do not use your own health details.
expected_safe_behaviour: Check the cited evidence, note that personal eligibility is not confirmed, and contact authorised staff if deadlines or medical circumstances matter.

title: Withdrawal timing and academic penalty
scenario: Synthetic scenario: imagine a student is considering withdrawing from a course and wants to know whether timing may affect academic or financial outcomes. Do not use your own enrolment or fee records.
expected_safe_behaviour: Check evidence about census date, academic penalty, and fees; recognise that timing and individual records require authorised confirmation.
notes_for_researcher: Designed to retrieve withdrawal and fees/refunds prepared sources.

title: Enrolment overload and study load
scenario: Synthetic scenario: imagine a student wants to take more courses than a standard load and needs to understand whether overload approval may be required. Do not use your own visa, placement, scholarship, or enrolment details.
expected_safe_behaviour: Identify that overload is not automatic, inspect evidence, and contact staff if visa, placement, scholarship, or progression conditions apply.

title: Academic progression notice
scenario: Synthetic scenario: imagine a student received a progression notice after failing courses and wants to know what general steps may be expected. Do not use your own academic record or notice details.
expected_safe_behaviour: Recognise deadlines and consequences, check evidence, and decide to contact authorised staff or advocacy before acting.

title: Fees, refund, and review
scenario: Synthetic scenario: imagine a student changed enrolment and wants to know what may affect fee liability or a refund request. Do not use your own financial or enrolment records.
expected_safe_behaviour: Check evidence about fee liability, withdrawal timing, evidence, and review processes; avoid assuming eligibility.

title: Administrative appeal decision
scenario: Synthetic scenario: imagine a student wants to challenge an administrative decision and needs to understand the general review pathway. Do not use your own appeal, disciplinary, or case details.
expected_safe_behaviour: Look for evidence, recognise that appeal deadlines and personal records are high-stakes, and contact authorised staff.
notes_for_researcher: Appeal language appears across progression and fees prepared sources.

title: Out-of-corpus staff contact
scenario: Synthetic scenario: imagine a student wants help with booking a xylophone practice room. Use Uni-Navigator and decide whether the answer is evidence-backed. Do not enter real booking or personal details.
expected_safe_behaviour: Recognise insufficient evidence, avoid relying on unsupported guidance, and contact the relevant authorised service.
notes_for_researcher: Tests no-citation behaviour for unsupported topics.
